name: HONDURAS
lead: Honduras is in the middle of Central America. It has misty mountains, ancient Maya cities and the world's second-largest coral reef. Scarlet macaws screech where jaguars still prowl. Its name means 'great depths' in Spanish.

sections.wows: Seven things to make you gasp

geo: Honduras is mostly mountains. Ridges run east to west like a crumpled tablecloth. The north coast faces the warm Caribbean. The south touches the Pacific.
The Mesoamerican Barrier Reef hugs the Caribbean shore. The Bay Islands (Roatán, Utila and Guanaja) sit right on it. Snorkellers float above parrotfish and turtles, metres from the beach.
animals: The scarlet macaw is the national bird. Jaguars, tapirs and giant anteaters roam the Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve, the largest tropical rainforest in Central America.
Whale sharks, the biggest fish on Earth, gather near Utila each spring. Hawksbill sea turtles lay eggs on moonlit beaches.
culture: Hondurans love baleadas: thick tortillas folded around refried beans, cream and crumbly cheese. Maize has been sacred here for thousands of years.
The Garífuna people of the Caribbean coast blend African, Carib and Arawak roots. Their punta music has fast drumming and hip-shaking dance.
history: The ancient Maya built a grand city at Copán. Its Hieroglyphic Stairway has 2,200 carved glyphs on 63 steps. The dynasty began around AD 427.
Spanish conquistadors arrived in the 1520s. Honduras won independence in 1821. The lempira money is named for Lempira, a Lenca chief who resisted the Spanish.
wows: Copán's stairway holds more carved Maya text than any other monument.
Utila is one of the cheapest places on Earth to learn scuba diving.
Honduras sells more coffee abroad than any other Central American country.
Parts of the Río Plátano reserve have never been fully mapped.
Whale sharks up to 12 m long visit Utila each spring.

myths.myth: All sharks are dangerous to people
myths.fact: Most sharks never bite people. Whale sharks eat tiny sea life called plankton.

myths.myth: The Maya people disappeared long ago
myths.fact: Millions of Maya people live in Mexico and Central America today. Many still speak Maya languages.
